review.notes:
The pre-errata cdb text matches lineage v5 (LCYW-EN019, 2012-09-29) exactly, so the recorded chain starts there; the earlier transitions v0 (MRD-075, 2002) through v4 (DPYG-EN006, 2009) are wording modernisations of the same Tribute-for-half-ATK effect and predate the baseline implementation, so they are not recorded as changes. One further script difference is NOT text-driven and is not recorded as its own change: the modern script gates the Release cost on s.cfilter (c:GetAttack()>0) while the pre-errata script passes nil, so the historical implementation permits Tributing a 0-ATK monster for 0 damage. No source in the packet dates that refinement; it is carried by the baseline implementation, which every pre-2014-06-27 snapshot selects anyway, so it does not need its own (blocking) unresolved-chronology entry. The second upstream code 511004015 is 'Catapult Turtle (Anime)' - a different card with three anime-only effects - and is excluded rather than folded in as an artwork variant.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Catapult Turtle). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved (general rule only) at Edison, unresolved (general rule only) at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the once-per-turn text (DL18-EN001, Duelist League 18 participation cards)

event.historical_text: You can Tribute 1 monster; inflict damage to your opponent equal to half the Tributed monster's ATK on the field.
event.modern_text: Once per turn: You can Tribute 1 monster; inflict damage to your opponent equal to half the Tributed monster's ATK on the field.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the Tribute-for-damage Ignition effect became a hard once per turn. The modern script carries e1:SetCountLimit(1) and pre-errata/c511000228.lua does not, so the historical card can Tribute monsters for damage repeatedly in one turn. EdisonFormat.com records the same period behaviour independently.

rulings_check.difference: Era: the Tribute-for-damage Ignition effect has no use limit, so it can be activated repeatedly in a turn as long as a monster can be Tributed each time; modern: hard once per turn.
